tasks.title: Extract Ralph utilities and add dynamic task loader
tasks.description: Extract the shared Ralph task-file, dependency-validation, sorting, and context-assembly helpers into stable modules and introduce `RalphTaskLoader` on top of them. The delivered capability is that Build dynamic tasks can be loaded from `tasks.json` as ordered executable work without relying on the legacy loop body to parse or validate the file.
acceptanceCriteria: `RalphTaskLoader` reads `tasks.json`, applies the existing normalization defaults, validates `dependsOn`, sorts tasks by the current order rules, and returns a linear executable Build task list
Shared helper exports for `readTasks`, `sortTasksByOrder`, `findNextPendingTask`, dependency validation, and `buildTaskContext` remain available through the existing compatibility surface
Loader-focused tests cover valid loading, missing dependency detection, circular dependency detection, and aggregate-mode progress reset without changing `tasks.json` schema
tasks.notes: Keep loader responsibilities limited to reading, validating, sorting, and shaping executable tasks; do not move next-task selection into the loader.

tasks.title: Implement Ralph single-task handler on shared task runtime
tasks.description: Implement `RalphTaskHandler` as a shared task-runtime handler that executes exactly one Build task with the existing retry, failure classification, WIP handling, learning capture, and persistence behavior. The delivered capability is that a future StageRunner can execute one Ralph task through `TaskHandlerRegistry` while preserving current Build reliability semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: A Ralph-specific task kind is registered through the shared task-runtime registry and executes one loaded Build task through the `TaskHandler` contract
`RalphTaskHandler` preserves current retry behavior, `categorizeFailure` and `FAILURE_CATEGORY_CONFIGS`, WIP resume handling, task progress persistence, and learning capture for one task
Session-failure results are treated as failed task attempts and remain governed by task-owned retry or pause policy rather than by the session runtime
Focused handler tests cover success, retryable AC failure, non-retryable dependency failure, timeout-with-WIP, and `session_failed` outcomes
tasks.notes: The handler owns one task's full lifecycle, including retries and side effects; do not push retry or pause policy back up into the runner layer.

tasks.title: Delegate legacy Ralph loop through loader and handler
tasks.description: Refactor `runRalphLoop()` and `RalphExecutor` into compatibility orchestrators that load tasks once, apply the existing loop semantics, and delegate each task execution to `RalphTaskHandler`. The delivered capability is that current BuildStageRunner and direct test callers keep using the same public API while the authoritative load and execute logic lives behind the new split runtime.
acceptanceCriteria: `runRalphLoop()` delegates task loading to `RalphTaskLoader` and single-task execution to `RalphTaskHandler` while preserving `skipTaskIds`, `onlyTaskId`, deadlock detection, and all-tasks-already-passed behavior

Compatibility exports `RalphExecutor`, `runRalphLoop`, `setAcpSessionRunner`, `resetAcpSessionRunner`, `readTasks`, `sortTasksByOrder`, `findNextPendingTask`, and `categorizeFailure` continue to work for existing callers
Build dynamic task behavior remains unchanged for task order, `dependsOn` semantics, failure-is-terminal loop behavior, timeout/session-failure handling, WIP commit flow, and aggregate task reporting
`BuildStageRunner` stays on the existing public Ralph execution path and does not switch to config-driven generic StageRunner mode in this task
tasks.notes: Preserve the current event names and loop result shape. This task must not migrate WorkflowEngine or default StageRunner registration.

tasks.title: Lock Ralph split behavior with focused regression coverage
tasks.spec: specs/ralph-task-execution/spec.md#Requirement: REQ-RTE-001 Task attempts consume session failure results
tasks.description: Add or update focused tests that prove the new loader, handler, and legacy wrapper preserve Ralph behavior at the utility, single-task, and compatibility-loop boundaries. The delivered capability is that future StageRunner unification work can rely on direct contract coverage without silently regressing Build task semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: Focused tests pass for loader ordering and dependency validation, handler success and failure paths, and legacy loop compatibility behavior including `onlyTaskId`, checkpoint recovery, validation failure, and deadlock handling
Focused tests prove `session_failed` results fail the current task attempt, do not mark the task passed, and remain subject to Ralph retry or pause policy
Existing Ralph-facing tests that import compatibility helpers continue to pass without changing the public helper names they use
tasks.notes: Prefer focused deterministic tests at the new boundaries instead of broad workflow rewrites.
